diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the second equality is because $\Vert A\Vert^{-1}A=U^\top V$

issues.failure_explanation: The lifting is A = ||A|| U^T V, so <u,Av> = ||A|| <Uu,Vv>. A critical value sigma of SV(A,P,Q) therefore corresponds to a critical cosine sigma/||A|| for (P~,Q~), not sigma. The remark states arccos(sigma) and so is false unless ||A|| = 1. The same proof also shows the optimal values are related by lambda* = ||A|| delta*.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, $\sigma$ is a $(P,Q)$-singular value of $A$ if and only if $\arccos(\sigma)$ is a critical angle between $\wt P$ and $\wt Q$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace arccos(sigma) by arccos(sigma/||A||) in the remark, or normalise A to spectral norm 1.
issues.overall_effect: The stated dictionary between Pareto/cone singular values and critical angles of the lifted cones is wrong by a scale factor. The theorem's solution-pair equivalence and the NP-hardness reduction are unaffected.
issues.title: Remark on singular values vs critical angles omits the factor ||A||
issues.why_classification: It is a one-line local correction that preserves every substantive claim and result.

issues.failure_explanation: Nash pairs are defined with global inequalities over all unit u in P and v in Q. For fixed v, minimising a linear function over P intersected with the unit sphere is convex only when the optimal value is negative. Otherwise there are local minimisers that are not global in that block. Example: P = R^2_+, A = I, v = (1,2)/sqrt5. Then u = e_2 is a local minimiser in u of <u,Av>, but it is not a global minimiser because u = e_1 gives a smaller value. So (e_2, v) can be a local minimum of SV that fails the Nash inequality. The claim is true for solution pairs but false for local minima in general.

failure_location.quote: Observe also that any solution pair and all local minima of $\SV(A,P,Q)$ are Nash pairs.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the statement to solution pairs, or to local minima with negative value, where the block subproblems are convex.
issues.overall_effect: The general statement about local minima is unreliable. The proof of pro:nonnegative_case_SVcones uses only the correct part (solution pairs are Nash pairs), so its conclusions are unaffected.
issues.title: False claim that all local minima of SV(A,P,Q) are Nash pairs
issues.why_classification: A local restriction of the sentence repairs it, and no later result relies on the false part.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For each of the $d$ non-zero entries of $A$, we might have to branch up to a desired precision

issues.failure_explanation: The objective <u,Av> = sum over all (i,j) of A(i,j) u_i v_j involves every nonzero entry. With Omega limited to positive entries, the displayed problem 'equivalent to' (eq:SVconesineq) drops all negative entries, which are exactly the ones that make the optimal value negative. The reformulation is therefore not equivalent, and the McCormick bound would not bound lambda*. The text itself speaks of 'non-zero entries', so Omega should be {A(i,j) != 0}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define Omega as the set of nonzero entries of A.
issues.overall_effect: The stated equivalence, and the lower-bound and complexity discussion built on it, are wrong as written. The method and the reported experiments are unaffected once the index set is corrected.
issues.title: McCormick reformulation restricts the index set to positive entries of A
issues.why_classification: It is a local definitional fix; the construction and its guarantees are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: min(c,0) has nonpositive entries, so x = min(c,0)/||min(c,0)|| is nonpositive. It is infeasible for x >= 0 unless it is zero. The optimal solution is x = -min(c,0)/||min(c,0)|| = max(-c,0)/||max(-c,0)||, which puts weight on the negative entries of c. The written formula also gives objective value +||min(c,0)|| > 0, which is not a minimum.

failure_location.quote: It can be easily checked that the optimal solution is $x = \frac{\min(c,0)}{\|\min(c,0)\|}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the formula by x = max(-c,0)/||max(-c,0)||.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised closed-form update for the nonnegative-orthant case of the alternating optimization subproblems is incorrect as stated. The general subproblem solved via Gurobi is unaffected.
issues.title: Closed-form solution of the nonnegative-orthant subproblem has the wrong sign
issues.why_classification: A single local correction fixes it, and the algorithm and its stated guarantees are unaffected.
